static_traits.name: Chen Boan
static_traits.educational_background: High school graduate (saving money for college)
static_traits.social_status: Interpersonal relationships without obvious problems; having a few friends but not yet sharing these feelings with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no previous psychotherapy or other psychological treatment history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, acceptable logic; neutral attitude, cooperative; tending toward self-deprecation and negative self-talk, frequently using negating labels (e.g. 'I am not smart enough')

basic_info.main_problem: I feel I am not good enough and doubt my intelligence, especially when it comes to saving money for college.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these feelings of inferiority are hindering my focus on my goals and affecting my self-esteem.
growth_experiences: During high school, academic performance was 'just average', which started forming doubts about my own intelligence; when recalling high school grades I often anticipate I will also perform poorly in college, and this experience became the main reference point for current self-doubt.

After starting hotel night-shift work, gradually learning to manage time better; although confidence in college learning is still lacking, improved time management provides a potential resource for balancing learning and work in the future.

core_beliefs: I am not worthy of college / success.

special_situations.event: Whenever thinking of saving money for college and my own future prospects
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not smart enough, it is not worth investing time and money in going to college.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to push negative thoughts away; burying oneself in work and continuing to save money to avoid facing self-doubt.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am too stupid; going to college is not worth it either.

special_situations.event: Recalling that high school grades were just 'average'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I did not get good grades in high school, I will fail in college too.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Lowering expectations of university, avoiding discussing academic planning with others to avoid being evaluated.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will not test well in college either.

special_situations.event: When lacking clear affirmation or 'proof' from others
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only with external recognition and reassurance do I have value or be considered capable.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Seeking comfort and reassurance from others; hesitant and indecisive, waiting for external validation before acting.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If no one says I can do it, then I cannot.

special_situations.event: When others (such as the counselor) point out their progress (such as improved time management ability)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Small improvements do not count; only significant achievements can prove I am not stupid.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating or ignoring positive evidence, emphasizing its tiny effect.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is no use; it changes nothing.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized and accepted by others for one's abilities, and to pursue the goal of attending university with peace of mind
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being seen as weak or stupid; fearing being negated after failure
defense_goal: Avoiding exposing vulnerability and needs (not confiding in friends) to maintain a sense of safety
Lowering expectations through self-deprecation, thereby reducing shame and anxiety when failing
Maintaining emotional caution and distance, reducing the risk of being evaluated

object_relations.self_representation: A self not smart enough, prone to failure
object_relations.object_representation: Others who may judge and look down on oneself and see it as weakness (such as friends/peers)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others affirm one's strengths or progress (such as improved time management skills)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiencing affirmation as 'inconsequential or not counting'; worrying the other is just comforting, and will eventually see through one's 'not being smart'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gentle but reserved tone; first showing understanding then citing examples starting with 'but' to negate positive feedback, highlighting its limitations and non-generalizability.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to share troubles with friends or seek support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing others will see oneself as weak and judge accordingly (transference: projecting inner shame onto others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Adopting avoidance and short answers; emphasizing 'I do not want to trouble others'; cautious and restrained tone, declining further self-disclosure.

manifestations: Believing 'I am too stupid; going to college is not worth it either', questioning the value of long-term effort (saving money / going to college)
Feeling overwhelmed when the goal only focuses on the endpoint; difficulty experiencing the meaning of present effort
Having friends but unwilling to share inferiority and worries
Worrying about being seen as 'weak' and shutting oneself off
outcomes: Social support insufficient; increased emotional burden
Negative self-narrative hard to correct by outside input

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: Frequent self-blame and labeling ('I am not smart enough')
Cautious and timid in conversation, seeking external 'proof' to confirm self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Treats 'only good grades deserve college' as an absolute standard
Takes external evaluation as the main condition of worth, ignoring the value of one's own efforts

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Worrying friends will think oneself weak, thus unwilling to share true feelings
Attributes shame in advance to others' possible evaluations

exception_events.target_problem: When thinking of college savings and future prospects, the client usually shows intense self-denial and negative self-talk, leading to decreased motivation.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Over the past six months, the client kept doing night-shift work and saving money for college as planned, not yet fully interrupting the saving behavior because of negative self-talk.
exception_events.reason: Clues: clear medium- and long-term goals (saving money for university) and a fixed work rhythm provided external structure; at the same time, night-shift work promoted the formation of time management habits, helping to maintain behavioral continuity.

exception_events.target_problem: When facing doubts about their own intelligence, the client usually concludes they will find it hard to succeed academically, which further lowers confidence and motivation.
exception_events.unique_outcome: After starting night-shift work, the client learned to manage time better, able to arrange and balance work tasks more methodically, forming realistic and feasible self-management experience.
exception_events.reason: Clue: different situations and approaches — the actual demands of night-shift work prompted practicing priority management and time scheduling, producing observable task completion and a sense of order.

positive_force: Persisted in saving money for university for six consecutive months; has a degree of self-discipline and goal persistence
Night-shift work trained time management ability (transferable executive functioning)
Proactively seeking psychological counseling to improve the current situation, with clear motivation to change
Has several friends; potential social support resources exist
negative_force: Self-labeling and overgeneralization ('I am stupid', 'I will fail at university too')
Negating positive evidence; difficulty internalizing one's own progress
Overly reliant on external affirmation to judge self-worth
Worried about being seen as weak, avoids help-seeking and expression
Frequent negative self-talk erodes motivation and self-esteem

target_behavior.behavior: Negative self-talk and self-deprecation (e.g. 'you are not smart enough / you will not succeed')
antecedent: Thinking of saving money for college and future prospects
Recalling high school grades being 'just average'
target_behavior.core_reason: The inner core belief 'I am not smart enough', and using self-deprecation to preemptively lower expectations to avoid the shame and anxiety failure brings
target_behavior.function: Escaping uncertainty and failure anxiety; retreating preemptively for short-term psychological relief
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased motivation and impaired self-esteem; affecting continued saving and investment in college preparation

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids seeking support from friends and expressing vulnerable feelings
antecedent: Being asked whether one shares troubles with others
Thinking others may see them as weak
target_behavior.core_reason: Shame and fear of being evaluated; projecting inner inferiority onto others
target_behavior.function: Avoiding negative evaluation; maintaining self-protection and a sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Lack of social support; inner accumulated stress; negative thought loops reinforced
